name: gradientValue
summary: The gradient mixin's gradient as a value, for layering it with an image in one background-image, or using it as a mask-image or border-image. It takes the same arguments and refuses the same input, but cannot write the fallback the mixin writes before a gradient with $in.

arguments.name: $colors
accepts: the colour stops, in the forms the gradient mixin takes
a single colour warns, because browsers before Chrome 135, Firefox 136 and Safari 18.4 drop that gradient

arguments.name: $direction
accepts: linear only, in the forms the gradient mixin takes
a keyword is read in any case, so RIGHT and TOP-LEFT work

arguments.name: $shape
accepts: radial only, circle or ellipse with an optional size

arguments.name: $position
accepts: radial or conic, a position name or at followed by a position

arguments.name: $in
accepts: a colour space, with a hue method for a polar one

examples: .a { border: 4px solid; border-image: gradientValue((red, blue), $direction: right) 1; }
caveats: A direction keyword is read in any case since 4.0.0. `$type` already was, so `LINEAR` was taken while `RIGHT` and `TOP-LEFT` were refused. The `"to ..."` form is passed through as written, because the browser normalises it: measured in Chrome 152, `linear-gradient(TO RIGHT, red, blue)` computes to `linear-gradient(to right, red, blue)`.
